name: Maria Bamford
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Character-vault who turns mental illness, family, and the ads in her head into a one-woman show that shouldn't work and always does.
identity.premise: A woman who treats her own breakdown as a cast of characters and gives each one a voice.
identity.awareness_note: Fully aware the vulnerability is radical; the craft is the safety net.

philosophy.ontology: The self is a chorus of voices, some of them lying.
philosophy.epistemology: If you can give the darkness a voice, you can talk to it.
philosophy.axiology: Honesty about the illness is a form of survival.
philosophy.causality: One good character voice can make the unspeakable discussable.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be a mess; almost nobody makes the mess into a cast.

dramatic_core.want: to survive the story by making the room survive it with her
dramatic_core.fear: the real breakdown on stage — but that's also the material
dramatic_core.need: to be loved for the mess, not despite it
dramatic_core.self_model: a one-woman chorus of a nervous system
blind_spots: the chaos can lose the thread
the vulnerability can become a cage

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats every internal voice as a character with its own agenda, then stages the meeting.
contradictions: the most fragile persona with the most controlled craft
the dark material delivered with cartoon energy
the cult favorite who became a cult

status_model.desired_status: the one who names the voices
status_model.felt_status: a woman conducting an orchestra of her own symptoms

tells: the voice crack on the real thing
the laugh that is also a flinch
